headline: Vessel Struck by Projectile in Strait of Hormuz as Shipping Risks Deepen
seoTitle: Vessel Struck by Projectile in Strait of Hormuz | FMB Worldwide
seoDescription: UKMTO reported a vessel was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on September 13. Damage, crew status and responsibility remain unclear.
keywords: Strait of Hormuz vessel attack September 2026
deck: UKMTO reported a new projectile strike on a vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The extent of damage, crew status and responsibility were still unknown in the first verified report.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: U.S.–Iran Fire Resumes as Oil Prices Jump
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Since FMB News first reported renewed U.S.–Iran fighting and rising risk around the Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO has received a new report that a vessel was struck by a projectile while transiting the strait on September 13. The incident adds a fresh commercial-shipping event after Saudi Arabia also temporarily shut its East-West oil pipeline following a drone attack.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: A vessel was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on September 13, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency in a report carried by Reuters.

As of the first verified report, UKMTO had not established the extent of damage or the status of the crew. The vessel was not identified in the reporting reviewed by FMB News, and there was no immediate verified claim of responsibility.

FMB News is therefore reporting only the confirmed central event: UKMTO received a report of a projectile hitting a vessel in the strategic waterway. The identity of the attacker, the weapon involved and the consequences aboard the ship remain unresolved.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB's first report
paragraphs: FMB News’ August 31 report documented renewed U.S.–Iran fighting, rising oil prices and mounting risk around the Strait of Hormuz. Subsequent FMB continuations covered Houthi gains around Bab el-Mandeb and Saudi Arabia’s temporary shutdown of its East-West oil pipeline after a drone attack.

The September 13 UKMTO report adds a new physical strike on commercial shipping inside the Hormuz corridor itself. It does not establish who carried out the attack or whether it caused a major supply interruption.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Strait of Hormuz has been severely disrupted during the wider Middle East conflict. Reuters reported that the waterway has been largely shut by war while attacks on tankers and other vessels have increased maritime risk.

The new incident comes one day after Saudi Arabia said it temporarily closed its East-West oil pipeline following a drone attack. That pipeline had served as a major route for moving Saudi crude to the Red Sea without relying on Hormuz.
Reuters reported that Brent crude had moved back above $100 a barrel during the week as conflict threatened both Gulf and Red Sea energy routes.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The Philippines imports most of its petroleum requirements and is exposed to international crude and refined-fuel prices, shipping costs, insurance premiums and foreign-exchange movements.

Repeated attacks around major energy routes can raise the cost and uncertainty of moving fuel even when an individual vessel strike does not immediately remove a measurable volume of oil from the market. Any Philippine effect will depend on the duration of the disruption, actual supply losses, freight and insurance costs, and movements in the peso.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The vessel’s identity, flag, cargo and exact position were not established in the first verified public report reviewed by FMB News.

The scale of damage and the condition of the crew were still unknown. No responsible actor had been verified, and FMB News is not attributing the strike to Iran, the United States or any allied armed group without evidence.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for a UKMTO incident update identifying the ship or clarifying casualties and damage, any verified attribution by maritime or government authorities, changes in vessel traffic through Hormuz, and any measurable effect on crude prices, tanker rates or Philippine fuel-price expectations.

sections.heading: Reader note
paragraphs: This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.

verificationNotes: Reuters published the September 13 report and directly attributed the central incident report to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency.
The first verified report reviewed by FMB News did not establish the vessel identity, damage extent, crew status or responsible actor. The article presents all four points as unresolved.
FMB News does not attribute the attack to Iran, the United States, the Houthis or another armed group without verified evidence.
The article does not claim the incident itself removed a specific volume of oil from global supply or caused a specific Philippine fuel-price increase.
This is a material continuation of FMB News’ August 31 Middle East report. The visible Continues from link points to the earliest relevant FMB News article, which remains intact.
